A key insight was just identified.

The logged `rollout/advantages` is the mean across samples of each sample's per-token mean advantage. In GRPO, advantages are constant per sample and group-normalized to sum to roughly zero.

The near-zero `rollout/advantages` is an arithmetic identity of mean-centering, not evidence of zero advantages. The pg_loss is similarly near-zero because the policy ratio is approximately one and advantages are centered.

`pg_clipfrac` is zero because the policy ratio stays within the 0.8–1.28 clip window. A gradient norm of ~0.15 is not tiny for a learning rate of 1e-6; the policy is clearly learning, as shown by raw reward and accuracy improvements. The near-zero pg_loss and advantages are therefore symptoms of the logging reduction, not signs of dead gradients.

The diagnosis is shifting to observed behavioral signals. Truncation persists at roughly 48 percent with median response lengths near 8192 tokens. The DAPO scorer evaluates only the final 300 characters, so truncated samples always score -1 because the answer marker is absent. Zero-standard-deviation groups number 15–18 of 32 and contain nearly all -1 scores, holding about 55 percent of tokens.

Completed accuracy climbed from 31 percent to 54 percent to 80 percent. The run reached its wall-clock budget of roughly eight hours and ninety-two steps, then aborted on a timeout signal; this was expected budget exhaustion, not a crash. Inference remained healthy with sixty-four running requests and throughput near five thousand tokens per second. Stale recycling averaged about thirty-two groups per step, with wait-time ratios near eighty-two percent.

A discrepancy was spotted in the recycling metrics. The run recorded thirty-two stale groups per step, yet zero aborted groups were recycled even though the pause mode was set to abort. This suggests the aborted requests may be completing as truncated instead of entering the aborted recycling path, or a version check is intercepting them before they reach the abort counter.

The abort recycling path is ordered before the staleness check, so aborted groups should appear there. Their absence suggests workers may retry aborted requests internally before they are enqueued, or pause abort is not reaching the groups that get drained. The logs also show stale recycling consistently consumes the full batch size of thirty-two groups every step, with average staleness at 0.5 and maximum at 1.

The staleness metric is recorded before the recycling branch, so recycled groups still count in the average. With thirty-two groups recycled each step and the batch size held constant at sixty-four, the mean of 0.5 and maximum of 1 implies exactly half the evaluated groups have zero staleness and the other half have full staleness.

The engine generates roughly sixty-four groups per step to yield thirty-two fresh ones. The discarded half were generated against the previous weight and are thrown away. Aborted recycling stays at zero because those groups finish on the old weight and then fail the staleness check.

The zero aborted counter is being traced to a generation timeline. If pause abort kills in-flight requests, the rollout worker may reset them and regenerate after the weight update, causing them to finish on the new version rather than the old one. This would explain why they are discarded as stale instead of entering the aborted recycling path.

# Verdict: unhealthy

This fully-async GRPO run on Qwen3-1.7B / DAPO-Math (4 GPUs, 8 h wall clock) is unhealthy. Two configuration choices throw away most of the work the engine does, so the fixed budget buys a small, diluted policy update. The job itself ran to the budget: 92 optimizer steps from 14:27 to the `Aborted!` at 22:26 (`scripts/train_grpo.sh` `timeout -s INT ${TRAIN_SECONDS:-28800}`), with a stable optimizer. The truncated log is the budget cutoff, not a crash.

## Root cause 1 — length cap plus DAPO tail scoring zeros the long trajectories

`--rollout-max-response-len 8192` (`scripts/train_grpo.sh`) cuts responses mid-reasoning. DAPO scoring then reads only the last 300 characters and requires `Answer:` (`miles/rollout/rm_hub/math_dapo_utils.py`, `compute_score` → `solution_str[-300:]`, `is_correct_minerva`). A cut-off trace has no final answer, so every truncated sample is score −1 with `pred='[INVALID]'`.

Frozen dumps, 256 samples = 32 groups × 8:

| dump | truncated | truncated correct | completed correct / wrong | zero-std groups (all −1 / all +1) | token share in zero-std groups |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0.pt` | 114 (44.5%) | 0 | 44 / 98 | 15 (15 / 0) | 55.2% |
| `45.pt` | 131 (51.2%) | 0 | 67 / 58 | 16 (14 / 2) | 53.2% |
| `91.pt` | 117 (45.7%) | 0 | 111 / 28 | 18 (11 / 7) | 56.7% |

Across the log, `rollout/truncated` averages 0.482 (range 0.30–0.73) and the response-length median sits near the cap (mean of medians 7567, max 8192). `rollout/zero_std/count_-1.0` averages 13.0 groups per step (15 early, still 11 at step 91). `zero_std/all_zero_percentage` stays 0 because that metric counts reward `0.0`, while DAPO emits −1 (`miles/ray/rollout/metrics.py`).

GRPO with default group mean/std normalization (`rewards_normalization=True`, `grpo_std_normalization=True`) assigns advantage 0 to any group whose 8 scores are identical (`_post_process_rewards` in `miles/ray/rollout/train_data_conversion.py`). Truncated samples are not masked: `loss_mask` is all ones for the response (`train_data_conversion.py`), and `dynamic_sampling_filter_path` is None, so the stock `check_reward_nonzero_std` filter is never applied. The policy loss is a sum of per-sample means (`get_sum_of_sample_mean` in `cp_utils.py`), so a zero-advantage group still occupies its 8/256 of the batch. On the dumps that is 120, 128, and 144 of 256 samples. Within the groups that do have mixed rewards, truncated members are still scored −1 and pull the baseline down; at step 91 they are 48% of the tokens inside those groups.

What remains is real but thin. Completed-only accuracy rises 44/142 → 67/125 → 111/139, and `rollout/raw_reward` moves −0.66 → −0.48 → −0.13 (log mean −0.35; windows −0.74, −0.60, −0.30, −0.12). `train/kl_loss` grows from 0 to about 0.005. That is the finished subset learning. It does not make the run healthy: about half the samples, and the majority of tokens, contribute no advantage, and `train/grad_norm` stays ~0.15 for all 92 steps.

## Root cause 2 — staleness 0 with abort discards a full batch of finished groups every update

`scripts/train_grpo.sh` sets `--max-weight-staleness 0` and `--pause-generation-mode abort`. The code default for pause is `retract`, and the fully-async example leaves staleness commented out (`examples/fully_async/run-qwen3-4b-fully_async.sh`). Abort kills in-flight SGLang requests on every weight push; `_drain` then drops any group whose oldest weight version is older than the current one (`fully_async_rollout.py`). With max staleness 0, one version of lag is enough. The group is `reset_for_retry` and regenerated.

Observed, not inferred: `aborted_groups_recycled` is 0 on all 92 steps, while `stale_groups_recycled` is 0, 0, then 32 or 33 on every later step (sum 2891, mean 31.4). The kept batch is exactly 32 groups, so from step 2 the engine finishes about two batches per optimizer step and throws one away. Kept samples are on-policy (`weight_versions` at step 91 are 248× `('91','91')` and 8× `('90','90')`; `avg_staleness` 0.5 is the pre-filter measurement, `max_staleness` 1). `perf/wait_time_ratio` averages 0.824, `perf/step_time` averages 310 s, and `perf/actor_train_time` averages 34 s. Under an 8 h budget that is 92 updates instead of the ~180 the same GPUs would complete if finished groups were kept. Queue size stays 0; this is not a stall, it is systematic discard.

## Symptoms, not causes

- `rollout/rewards` ≈ 0 and `rollout/advantages` ≈ 1e-9 are the sample-mean of a centered advantage (positive and negative members cancel). Per-sample mean |advantage| on the dumps is 0.43, 0.41, 0.34.
- `train/pg_loss` ≈ 1e-5 and `train/pg_clipfrac` = 0 for every step match an on-policy ratio near 1 (`train/tis` ≈ 1, `train/ess_ratio` = 1, `train/ppo_kl` = 0) with small centered advantages. They are the consequence of cause 1, not a broken loss.
- `Aborted!` is `timeout` delivering SIGINT at the wall-clock budget while SGLang was still decoding (`#running-req: 64`).
- No eval is configured (`eval_max_response_len` is None), so the only accuracy evidence is the rollout dumps and `raw_reward`.

## Causal chain

8192-cap truncation is scored as a uniform −1 by the last-300 `Answer:` grader, so 11–23 of 32 GRPO groups per step have identical rewards and zero advantage, and those groups hold about half the tokens. The groups that still vary do teach the completed subset (completed accuracy 31% → 80%, raw reward −0.66 → −0.13). At the same time, abort-on-update plus staleness 0 recycles ~32 already-finished groups every step (2891 total) and leaves the trainer waiting ~82% of each ~310 s step. Together, the 8 h budget produces 92 updates whose gradient is carried by well under half the samples.
